---
applyTo: "packages/genui/ui-judge/**/*"
---

Keep UI Judge a Rust-only crate. Its public API, model integration, tests, and user examples belong under `packages/genui/ui-judge`; do not add an npm package manifest, TypeScript facade, or JavaScript test suite back to this directory. The default feature set remains library-only. The `server` feature owns the `ui-judge-server` binary and HTTP process adapter. The existing ReactLynx fixture source is a runtime asset consumed by the repository's headless runner, not a JavaScript UI Judge API or test harness.

Keep the default crate-root API restricted to `judge_page`, `JudgePageRequest`, `UiJudgeResult`, and `UiJudgeError`; the `server` feature may additionally expose its server module. The request uses only standard-library field types and always performs visual-correctness scoring internally. `JudgePageRequest::include_geqi` may additionally run the four weighted GEQI dimensions against the same final screenshot; keep their identifiers, labels, criteria, order, and weights internal rather than exporting dimension-selection or prompt APIs. Do not export model clients, model options, runner types, screenshot helpers, prompts, parsers, GEQI dimension types, fixture helpers, or screenshot-comparison APIs.

Keep the feature-gated server protocol at `GET /health`, `POST /judge`, `POST /screenshot`, and `POST /compare`. The screenshot route accepts the same JSON request as `/judge`, returns the captured PNG as `image/png`, and skips VLM scoring, GEQI, and reference-image comparison. It must reuse the bounded headless capture worker; avoid model initialization when `steps` is empty, and use Agent SDK only to execute non-empty natural-language steps. The comparison route accepts exactly one `referenceImage` and one `renderedImage` multipart upload, applies the existing image limits, and runs only deterministic normalization, alignment, and pixel comparison; it must not initialize a model client or enqueue headless rendering. Read `LYNX_USE_PORT` with a default of `8080`, reject zero, and bind separate IPv4 and IPv6 unspecified listeners. Have `build.rs` generate an executable `start.sh` in the Cargo profile output directory that starts the colocated `ui-judge-server` binary, copy the target Lynx runtime and `lynx_core.js` into the same runnable output layout, and package those generated assets rather than recovering them independently in `build.sh`. Honor `LYNX_CORE_JS_PATH` as the build-time core-script source while retaining the platform-standard packaged destination name. The server binary should select the packaged runtime when the caller has not set `LYNX_LIB_PATH` or `LYNX_SDK_DIR`, so the launcher stays a simple colocated executable wrapper. Accept HTTP connections concurrently, and run at most four native Lynx page-capture futures (connection, navigation, steps, and capture) on one dedicated current-thread worker because the runner is thread-bound. Use a bounded capture queue and return `503` on backpressure. After capture, run VLM scoring and reference comparison concurrently across judge requests. Limit request bodies, release cancelled queued jobs, and gracefully drain the HTTP server and join the headless worker on SIGINT or SIGTERM. Treat a headless-worker panic as fatal: mark readiness unhealthy, initiate shutdown, and propagate the join failure from the server task.

Keep reference-image comparison inside the Rust crate and reachable through `JudgePageRequest::reference_image`. Preserve `reference` as textual model context; accept reference images as plain base64, base64 data URLs, or HTTP(S) URLs, with explicit compressed-byte, decoded-dimension, pixel-count, and allocation limits. After the final screenshot is captured, run the VLM evaluations and reference-image comparison as independent chains that share only the captured PNG. Every VLM evaluation always scores that single screenshot from `task` and textual `reference`; never send the reference image, alignment result, pixel diff, or deterministic similarity to a VLM. The reference-image chain must only load and normalize the baseline, align it with normalized cross-correlation, and compute block-based pixel differences and a diff image. Run bounded alignment and pixel-diff work off the current-thread runtime. Keep top-level `score`, `reason`, and `summary` owned by the visual-correctness VLM; keep each GEQI dimension's score, reason, summary, and error independent, preserve the 30/25/15/15 relative weighting normalized to a 0-100 result, and do not let a dimension failure overwrite the visual-correctness result. Report reference-image failures separately without overwriting VLM output, and preserve successful comparison diagnostics when VLM scoring fails. Expose only standard-type diagnostics on `UiJudgeResult`; keep alignment, comparison, artifact, prompt, and algorithm types private to the crate.

Preserve the former TypeScript reference-comparison semantics during migration work: successful alignment compares the overlap crop, fallback comparison normalizes both images to their minimum dimensions with fill-style resizing, and pixel distance compares all four raw RGBA channels. Penalizing non-overlap or premultiplying alpha is a separate metric change, not a migration cleanup. Keep CPU-heavy image work on a bounded shared Rayon pool behind a small shared semaphore; move each permit into the worker so timeout or cancellation cannot release capacity before the worker exits, return results over a cancellation-safe channel, and use cooperative cancellation checks in loops owned by UI Judge.

Do not modify or duplicate `lynx-headless-rust-test-runner` as part of UI Judge work. `judge_page` must accept only `file://`, `http://`, and `https://` URLs; reject bare paths and other schemes before initializing the model or headless runtime. Internally use the runner's existing navigation, DOM, selector tap, wait, and software screenshot APIs. Keep model creation, the headless Lynx connection, and the page lifecycle inside `judge_page`. Do not re-export `Lynx`, `Page`, or other runner implementation types or require callers to construct them. Keep `judge_page` compatible with sequential use on a Tokio current-thread runtime because the runner's native task pump and page state are bound to their creation thread. Preserve natural-language `steps` by using Agent SDK to choose selector taps and waits from the current DOM and screenshot; report swipe, scrolling, typing, and coordinate touch as unsupported because the existing runner does not expose them. Do not add Kitten-Lynx, Android, ADB, an emulator, Playwright, or a browser as a UI Judge runtime dependency.

Keep `JudgePageRequest::timeout` compatible with the former TypeScript API: it is a per-operation and per-step limit, not an overall request deadline. Connection, navigation, each natural-language step, final screenshot capture, visual-correctness scoring, each enabled GEQI dimension, and optional reference-image comparison each receive the full duration; document that distinction wherever the request API is shown.

Use Agent SDK for structured VLM evaluation. Keep any OpenAI-compatible transport adapter in Rust and use only the documented `UI_JUDGE_API_KEY`, `UI_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, `UI_JUDGE_MODEL`, `UI_JUDGE_API_STYLE`, and `UI_JUDGE_TIMEOUT_MS` model environment-variable inputs. Do not accept legacy Midscene- or OpenAI-prefixed variables, JSON init config, or model-family configuration, and do not add a Midscene runtime dependency. Keep unit tests deterministic with `UI_JUDGE_MODEL_RESPONSE_JSON`. The runtime-backed `headless_e2e` integration test is intentionally different: it must reject mock-response variables unconditionally. It must skip inside the test when `UI_JUDGE_API_KEY` is absent or empty; otherwise it must call the real model supplied through the injected model environment.

Keep 0-5 score normalization and typed page result structures in the Rust library. Keep top-level `score` as the backward-compatible visual-correctness result; expose the optional weighted aggregate separately as `geqi_score` from 0 through 100. Do not add result-file generation, a UI Judge PR-comment action, or a GitHub comment publishing workflow.

Keep concurrent-rendering coverage fixed-size and behavioral: submit four distinct fixture bundles through the production headless worker, validate each screenshot, and do not add duration, QPS, latency, or throughput assertions.

Keep the existing React Lynx fixture at `packages/genui/ui-judge/tests/fixtures/react`, because the unchanged headless runner reads that path. Build its `.lynx.bundle` into the ignored `.generated/` directory and never commit generated bundle binaries.
